chunks: From him, from Abu al-Kharaj al-Ansari, from Ali ibn Gharab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Cursed is he who casts his burden (or dependence) upon the people."

key_terms.أَلْقَى كَلَّهُ: Cast his burden/dependence, to rely entirely on others
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family
key_terms.مَلْعُونٌ: Cursed, one who is deprived of God's mercy

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to cast one's burden upon people in Islamic ethics?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*'s chapter on earnings, this hadith specifically critiques the practice of 'alqa al-kallah'—shifting one's burden or needs onto others—often interpreted as seeking sustenance without effort or imposing financial strain on the community. It underscores the Shia ethical emphasis on dignified self-sufficiency, warning that those who make themselves a burden to others incur a divine curse (*mal'un*), distinguishing between legitimate need and parasitic dependence.
